confirmed.title: Sheet outbox stops for every resident once 12 entries are skipped: skipped entries are never removed, and the script only ever reads the first 12 outbox documents
confirmed.scenario:
1. A new resident is added to the app's People list (residents/{rid}). This makes isMember() true, so their new app cases are written to sheetOutbox. The PCs have not yet added them to the response sheet's Residents tab, or never will now that the app is the main log. A resident whose People id differs from the sheet's id, or whose rid is not 6 digits, hits the same path.
2. Every 5 minutes logbookOutboxRun lists `sheetOutbox?pageSize=12`. With no orderBy, Firestore REST returns documents in __name__ (case id) order. For this resident's entries, logbookOutboxAdd_ returns `skipped` ('no resident … on the Residents sheet'), and those entries are never removed (only r.done is removed).
3. Once 12 or more skipped entries exist, each run reads the same first page. Any other resident's entry whose random 16-char id sorts after the 12th skipped id is never listed again.
4. A new intake logging a few cases a day reaches 12 skipped entries in a day or two. From then on, a growing share of all residents' app cases silently stop reaching the Case tab, Database, report and AY totals.
confirmed.consequence: New app cases from residents who ARE on the sheet never reach the response sheet. Sheet counts and the Grand Total fall behind the app, and the backup is missing those cases. Nothing fails visibly: skips are only console.warn, the run throws only for Database/sort errors so no failure email goes out, and the app shows the case as synced. As skipped entries pile up, almost nothing gets through.
confirmed.fix: In logbookOutboxRun, page through the whole outbox (pageSize up to 300, following nextPageToken). Pick the first BATCH entries that can be processed, passing over skipped ones (or keep skipped ids in a Script property and step past them). Also report skipped entries loudly: throw at the end of the run with the count and rids so Google's failure email reaches the owner, and/or show them in the nightly Totals report, so the PCs add the resident to the Residents tab. Add a paging test with more than 12 skipped entries.
verifier_fix:
The proposed fix is right in direction, with three changes.

1. **Don't page the whole outbox every 5 minutes.** Firestore bills one read per listed document. At 288 runs a day, 40 to 100 stuck entries would add 11,000 to 29,000 reads a day; a normal day is about 4,000 and the free tier is 50,000.
   - Better: build `io` (the Residents tab) first. Then use `runQuery`, filtered to rids the sheet knows (`rid IN [...]`, in chunks of 30), with `limit: LOGBOOK_OUTBOX_BATCH`.
   - Or: list by name with `pageToken`, but start each run where the last stopped. Keep a Script property cursor (`startAt`/`pageToken` past known-skipped ids, or the skipped ids themselves), and do a full rescan only every hour or so.
2. **Report skips once, not on every run.** Throwing on every 5-minute run would fail 288 executions a day. Instead:
   - Put the skipped count, rids and age of the oldest skipped entry into the nightly Totals check (`LOGBOOK_TOTALS_LAST`).
   - Make that check, or one daily run, throw when a skipped entry is older than about a day, so Google's failure email reaches the owner.
3. **Add a test** whose `list()` fake follows the real REST behaviour: ordered by name, capped at 12, at least 13 skipped entries, plus later entries from residents who are on the sheet. Assert that those later entries are delivered.

Separately, look at `nextRid` (evals/js/ui-admin.js): for YYYYNN rids it suggests last year's prefix plus one, which feeds this path.

confirmed.title: An edited Form response whose case came in by the workbook import comes back as a second case (and a re-import after a Form edit does the same)
confirmed.scenario:
Path A:
1. A resident's older Form response is already in the logbook from the Admin or Firetop workbook import (source 'import', createdAt = the sheet Timestamp). This covers most cases.
2. 'Allow response editing' stays ON (owner, 14 Oct). The resident opens their edit link and fixes a typo or a tag.
3. logbookInboxSubmit fires for the edit and sends formInbox/{responseId} with submittedAt = response.getTimestamp(), which is now the edit time (form-inbox.js line 10 states 'changes when the response is edited').
4. On the next open, mergeFormEntries finds no form case with formCaseId(responseId). isImportOf requires sameResponse(c.createdAt, e.submittedAt), but the two times are days apart, so it returns false. The response is saved as a new 'form' case.

Path B:
1. A response that came in through the inbox is edited later. mergeFormEntries keeps the case's first createdAt (line 94), while the sheet row's Timestamp becomes the edit time.
2. A later Admin workbook re-import runs withoutFormCases. Its sameResponse(row.createdAt, c.createdAt) no longer matches, so the row is imported again as a new 'import' case.
confirmed.consequence: The logbook holds two cases for one sheet row: the old imported copy, unedited, plus the edited one. Total cases, every tag on the response and the Total tags figure come out higher in the app than in the sheet. For example, an LSCS + spinal response counts 4 tags in the app against 2 in the sheet. This is exactly what residents compare, and the drift check then reports an extra row.
confirmed.fix: Match on the response's FIRST submit time, not the latest. Code.gs can read it from the Forms API (`createTime`, via UrlFetchApp with ScriptApp.getOAuthToken()) and send it as `firstSubmittedAt` (add the key to validFormEntry). isImportOf then compares imported createdAt with that value. For path B, record the latest submittedAt on the form case (for example in its importKey `form:<id>@…`) and have withoutFormCases match a row against either time. Until then, when an import case has the same date and the inbox entry is an edit, replace that import case rather than adding a second one.
verifier_fix:
The direction is right, but adjust the details:
(1) Keep `submittedAt` (the last submit time) and ADD `firstSubmittedAt` (the Forms API `createTime`, from forms.responses.get via UrlFetchApp with ScriptApp.getOAuthToken()). This needs explicit oauthScopes in appsscript.json: forms.responses.readonly, plus the existing forms.currentonly, script.external_request and script.scriptapp. The owner then authorises the script again. Add the key to validFormEntry in the rules and test with tools/test-rules.sh.
(2) Have isImportOf match the import's createdAt against EITHER time. Comparing only with createTime would break responses edited before the workbook import: their sheet Timestamp, and so the import createdAt, was the last edit time then, and they match today.
(3) When the match is an edit (firstSubmittedAt != submittedAt), don't just push it to `dupes`, because that drops the resident's edit. Update the import case in place instead: keep its doc id, keep reflectionId, reflectTag and tags, leave it alone if its updatedAt shows an app edit after the import, and record the response id on it so later edits find it.
(4) Path B: store the latest submittedAt on the form case (a field, or in the importKey). withoutFormCases should then match a row against either createdAt or that time.
(5) Do NOT ship the interim idea "same date + edit → replace the import case". Residents log several cases a day, so it would overwrite an unrelated case. And without createTime the app can't tell that an entry is an edit.
(6) Add tests: an edited response whose case came from the import, and a re-import after an edited inbox response. Accept that one case stays unmatched: a response edited both before and after the import.

confirmed.title: Deleting a new app case and then Undo (or a bin restore, or a delete rolled back) takes it out of the sheet outbox and never puts it back
confirmed.scenario:
1. A programme resident logs a case. createCase calls toSheet and sheetOutbox/{id} is queued. The sheet script picks entries up only every 5 minutes, and indefinitely later while offline, for example in theatre without signal.
2. Within that window the resident deletes the case: edit dialog Delete, or multi-select delete. This runs moveToBin, then removeCase, then offSheet([id]), which deletes sheetOutbox/{id}.
3. They tap Undo on the 'Case moved to the recycle bin' toast, or restore it from the bin later. restoreFromBin calls restoreCase(out), which writes the case back but never calls toSheet.
4. The same happens when watchDeletes/rollBack undoes a delete that failed or lost a conflict. offSheet has already run. rollBack either restores the case with restoreCase (failed) or keeps the other device's edit (conflict), and neither re-queues the entry.
5. The sheet script never sees the case.
confirmed.consequence: The case is in the app (and its counts) but never in the response sheet. App totals stay one ahead of the sheet's Case tab, Database and Grand Total for that resident, and the backup is missing the case. Offline, the delete and the restore can be hours apart and both still drop the entry.
confirmed.fix: Re-queue on restore. Export toSheet from ui-core, or give restoreCase an option `{ sheet: true }`. Call it from restoreFromBin for kind 'case' when the restored id is unchanged (not when bin.js gives it a new id), and from rollBack when the case is written back. outboxEntry already keeps only source app or paste, and the script's column-J marker check means a case that had already reached the sheet before the delete is not added twice. Add delete, then Undo, then 'entry back in sheetOutbox' to the sheetOutbox conflict scenario.
verifier_fix:
Re-queue on restore, as proposed, with three refinements:

1. Only re-queue cases created after the outbox went live. Add a constant such as `SHEET_OUTBOX_SINCE = Date.parse('2026-10-14')` in `sheet-outbox.js` and check it in `outboxEntry`, or at the restore call sites. Otherwise a bin restore of an older 'app'-source case, which has no `app:<id>` marker in column J, back-fills it or adds a duplicate of a row the resident also logged through the Form. The marker check only dedupes rows the outbox itself made.

2. In `rollBack`'s conflict branch (bin.js:110, `continue`), the case is not written back but `offSheet` has already run. Re-queue the version that was kept (the live copy in S.cases, or the server copy once it arrives) there too, not only where `restoreCase` runs.

3. In `restoreFromBin`, re-queue only when the id is unchanged (as proposed).

The re-queue must stay fire-and-forget with `.catch`, as `toSheet` already is. The rules have no update on `sheetOutbox`, so if the drop never ran and the entry still exists, the `setDoc` is denied, which is harmless.

Add to the `sheetOutbox` emulator scenario: create, then `moveToBin`, then `restoreFromBin`, then assert the entry is back. Also assert that restoring a pre-go-live case queues nothing.

confirmed.title: Admin import's count check shows 'N differ' for every resident who logged in the app since the outbox went live
confirmed.scenario:
1. After 14 Oct, the outbox adds app cases to the Case tab with `app:<id>` in column J, and the sheet's AY Totals count them.
2. An admin (or Firetop, re-importing missing rows) loads the workbook in Admin → Import.
3. parseCaseSheet skips the app: rows ('Made in the app'). countCheck(g.cases, totals) then compares only the imported rows with AY Totals, which include the app rows.
confirmed.consequence: Every resident with app cases shows a red 'N differ' even when the app and the sheet agree. The import's own app-vs-sheet parity check becomes useless, and a real mismatch, such as a missing or doubled row, is hidden among the false alarms.
confirmed.fix: Have parseCaseSheet also return the skipped app rows' categories, for example as `appCases` with rid and cats, and let countCheck add them to `got` when comparing with the Totals tab. Alternatively, check the totals against the logbook's own counts after the import (countCases(all), which ui-admin already computes for the summary) and not the imported subset.
verifier_fix:
Use the first option, not countCases(all). The logbook's counts aren't comparable to the sheet's Totals for three reasons:
- App edits and deletes never reach the sheet.
- Logbook cases with source paste, import or form differ from what the sheet holds.
- `all` is only known after Import runs, but the check is shown before Import, as a pre-import gate.

Concretely:
1. In parseCaseSheet, run app rows through the same category parsing (catCols, splitLabels, codeOf) and push `{ rid, cats, row }` into a separate `appRows` list. Keep them out of `cases`, so the importKey loop and the existing test that keys don't depend on app rows stay unchanged.
2. In readWorkbook, group appRows by rid and call `countCheck([...g.cases, ...(appByRid.get(g.rid) || [])], t)`.
3. Optionally, add a group (0 cases to import, check only) for a rid that has only app rows, so its Totals are checked too.
4. Optionally, show "N made in the app" next to the count.
5. Add an importer test: one Form row plus one app row against a Totals value of 2 gives ok.
